$comment: Putting the gateway between an MCP client and its servers.
TWO FILES ARE INVOLVED, and confusing them is the usual mistake.
upstream.json   the servers you already had. The gateway reads this.
client.json     what your editor reads. It names exactly one server:
cirvix, which proxies everything in upstream.json.
Both shapes below are shown in this one file for convenience. Split them
The gateway accepts an editor's config verbatim — `mcpServers` (Claude
Code, Cursor, Windsurf) or `servers` (VS Code) — so upstream.json is
usually the file you already have, unchanged. An entry named `cirvix` is
skipped, so pointing the gateway at a config that already includes it does
stdio transport only. An entry with no `command` is ignored.
$notes: Paths must be absolute. The editor launches the gateway from a working
directory you do not control, and a relative --servers path resolves
With CIRVIX_API_URL and CIRVIX_API_KEY the gateway attaches a daemon: it
pulls policy, registers the agent in the fleet inventory, opens a run that
every decision belongs to, and ships telemetry. --policy then becomes the
fallback used only until the first sync.
Without them the gateway still enforces, from the local rule set, and
writes decisions to ./.cirvix/audit.jsonl. Verify that chain with:
Give the endpoint a `member`-scoped API key. It needs decision:write and
agent:write and nothing more; an admin key on a laptop is an admin
